name: solve_reachable_pose_sequence
summary: Select complete chained-IK pose sequences with optional scoped arm/environment collision rejection.

generality.rationale: Task-independent pose sequences; collision validation currently requires world-mounted revolute serial chains and declared static box obstacles. Score reduced to reflect this implemented scope.
assumptions: Discrete chained IK across task-complete waypoints is a useful feasibility test.
limitations: Self checks cover non-adjacent active links only; other arms are stationary snapshots.
No gripper, fixed chassis, synchronized dual-arm or continuous collision certification, dynamics, motion execution or task-effect verification.
Without an explicit scene/model context, collision clearance remains unknown; observed maps can leave important unseen space.
tested_tasks: robotwin/press-stapler-aloha-agilex (selection behavior extracted from harness_v2 multi-arm planner)
Synthetic collision rejection and candidate continuation; recorded turn-switch geometry replay

level.rationale: Composes pair ranking and chained IK with scoped collision rejection for the complete joint sequence.

composition.strategy: Solve each complete candidate, reject sampled arm/obstacle overlaps when a context is supplied, and continue to other variants or arms.

provenance.failure_gap: Arm selection and whole-sequence reachability were trapped inside a linear-contact-specific wrapper and could not be reused by grasp or place tasks.
evidence: Qwen fixed on right_arm and brute-forced raw IK in iter_001 even though a left-arm complete sequence was available.
